02-training-data.task: Build the example training data, check its labels, and show one fresh wording suggestion for review.
02-training-data.example: 24 training examples; 3 validation examples; no shared observations
02-training-data.note: The tool builds the lesson's labeled examples. Model-generated wording stays separate for review.

03-build-lora.task: Create a small CPU model, attach a new LoRA adapter, and check which parameters can change.
03-build-lora.note: This is a tiny practice model, not the running Lightning model.

04-train-adapter.task: Train the small CPU adapter for 40 steps, save it, and compare loss before and after.
04-train-adapter.example: 40 training steps completed; adapter saved; frozen-weight check passed
04-train-adapter.note: The fixed CPU recipe runs on the host. It does not train or restart the serving models.

05-attach-and-serve.task: Reload the CPU adapter, check that it changes model output, and compare the existing serving aliases.
05-attach-and-serve.example: Adapter reload changes logits; base and specialist both answer
05-attach-and-serve.note: The CPU adapter is tested locally. The deployed specialist is a separate, existing adapter.

06-evaluate.task: Run the small evaluation and report actual scores, including malformed or incorrect answers.
06-evaluate.example: Candidate score: 0/3 can be a valid result; it means the model needs work
06-evaluate.note: PASS means the evaluation ran and recorded its results, not that the model is accurate.

07-specialist-tool.task: Use Switchyard to answer one general question with base and classify one observation with specialist; check routing and tool rules.
07-specialist-tool.example: General → base; classification → specialist; actual model IDs checked
07-specialist-tool.note: The model proposes an answer. Code decides whether that answer passes the rules.

08-agent-skills.task: Create the lesson's draft-report and describe-observation skills, then discover and load them.
08-agent-skills.example: Two skill files created; names, instructions, and version hashes checked
08-agent-skills.note: The tool writes the lesson templates. Edit the skill text to change what the next agent run is told to do.

09-agent-loop.task: Use the NVIDIA Relay skill to check the instrumented agent exercise: run it through Switchyard, capture tool/model events, and record an injected missing-evidence failure.
09-agent-loop.example: perceive → triage → draft → finish, or request_review when a check fails
09-agent-loop.note: The prepared code wraps model/tool calls using managed Relay APIs. Check actual lifecycle events, including the injected failure. OpenClaw launches the lesson; the inner loop uses base.

10-openshell-policy.task: Prepare the lesson policy files and test allowed and denied operations in the existing OpenClaw sandbox.
10-openshell-policy.example: List models: allowed; /health: denied; source write: denied; scratch write: allowed
10-openshell-policy.note: The live probes test the existing demo sandbox's policy. The newly written student policy is a separate exercise file, not deployed by this demo.

11-trace-and-improve.task: Inspect the failed Relay trace, verify the matching Gym reward rule, train a fresh tiny CPU policy with NeMo RL loss functions, and compare the result.
11-trace-and-improve.example: Missing evidence → reward 0; fresh RL updates → compare plan probabilities and replay
11-trace-and-improve.note: 40 CPU updates train a 12-parameter plan policy. Trace evidence explains the verifier rule; training uses fresh on-policy samples. No Lightning weights change.
